title: Signed within-visit systolic settling does not improve albuminuria discrimination across two independently sampled NHANES cycles
abstract: Conventional averaging discards the order of repeated blood-pressure readings. We tested whether third-minus-first systolic pressure adds albuminuria information beyond clinical risk factors, mean pressure and unsigned within-visit variability. Fixed source-only ridge models were developed in 5,284 NHANES 2009–2010 adults (545 single-urine ACR elevations) and tested without tuning in 4,634 independently sampled 2011–2012 adults (577 elevations). Adding signed settling to the baseline-plus-SBP-SD model reduced source out-of-fold AUC from 0.75558 to 0.75541. External AUC changed from 0.762534 to 0.762584: paired difference 0.000050 (95% conditional bootstrap CI −0.000185 to 0.000284). Joint source/target refitting gave a wider CI of −0.002633 to 0.000904. Neither the prespecified success rule nor the Brier criterion was met. This is a bounded negative existing-data result, not proof that all ordered BP patterns lack information.
